items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I said “Mom I’m playing with Miles Davis.” ... I had heard later on that Nina Simone was backstage saying things like “he’d better not steal my drummer... Tony Williams gave me the call to do this record date. And I walked into the studio... I played drums on the record, I played drums on “Miles Run

ctx.x: Well I’m wondering what the phone call to your mother was like when you decided to switch careers.

Hell. That’s the only thing, for want of a better word. Take into consideration the time. It was the sixties, the fifties and sixties. I’m a black American growing up in a certain kind of environment and the revolution wasn’t really going on when I was going to school, I’m talking about ’58, ’59. It wasn’t really prevalent then. There were no revolutionary activities around that time. Parents wanted their kids — I’m talking about Afro-American parents — wanted their kids to be doctors, lawyers, something with…
Gosh well she can at least brag to her neighbors perhaps.
